findings.citation: spec.md:161-162 — "That Manager's token, used against a real listing endpoint, returns that Tenant's own Client and does not return the seeded Tenant's Clients."
findings.note: The exclusion half of story 5 is vacuous. The seeded Tenant holds no Clients in the test baseline — V17's Demo Client is deleted by V54__trim_seed_to_test_baseline.sql:161 — so assertThat(clients).hasSize(1) plus the id check passes even against a fully tenant-blind listing. There is nothing to exclude, so that leg can never fail. Fix: create a Client in the seeded Tenant within the same test (managerToken() + POST /api/clients) and assert it is absent from the second-Tenant Manager's list. Verified independently by the orchestrator before the fix pass.

Loop bookkeeping rides along in the feature diff: the answered handover-approval item is deleted and docs/inbox/.gitkeep added, asked for by no story, decision or ticket. Not a code smell and not in source lines this feature changed — the orchestrator's own state-keeping, which the loop requires to live on a branch because it never pushes main. Left for the delivery report to explain rather than for the fixer to undo.

Duplicated Code: the inline post("/api/auth/login") + text block shape duplicates IntegrationTest.loginAs, which already returns the token and which line 60 of this same file uses. CollidingUsernameSignInApiTest.java:65 duplicates it again for a plain 200 assertion. The 401 case at CollidingUsernameSignInApiTest.java:44 is a legitimate exception, since loginAs asserts isOk().

Mysterious Name: bare UUID literal 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111 (the V2-seeded Default Tenant) with nothing naming it, where IntegrationTest.java:70-78 already establishes named SEEDED_* constants for exactly this.
Speculative Generality: OtherTenantLogin.userId is read by no caller anywhere in backend/src.

Duplicated Code: the Client-building block (five setters, literal name "Other Tenant Client") duplicates lines 88-93, where the file's own pattern is a private helper like newTenant/newAgent. The shared literal name also yields two same-named Clients across two fixture calls in one run.
